notes: Import a file from another account

entries.title: Import a file from another account
entries.detail: A file exported from another of your accounts now imports as your own tasks, with their subtasks and comments. Before, tabula kept them as the other account's tasks and could not save them.

entries.title: Import opens the file window in the Mac app
entries.detail: Settings › Data › Import is a Choose file… button now. In the Mac app, choosing from the old list opened no file window. tabula reads a file ending in .csv as CSV, any other as JSON.

entries.title: A long objective title wraps beside its tags
entries.detail: In Goals, a long objective title now wraps onto a second line, so its tags stay beside it and Share stays at the right, as on every other objective.

entries.title: Fold an objective in Goals
entries.detail: The box with the arrow before an objective's name folds it to its head and says how many key results it holds; press it again to open it. The box beside Objectives and Roadmap folds every objective at once, and opens them again. This device remembers which are folded.

entries.title: Enter saves a check-in
entries.detail: In the Check in window, press Enter to save the check-in, also in the note. Shift+Enter starts a new line in the note. Enter on Cancel still cancels.

entries.title: A key result lists its Jira epics
entries.detail: Under a key result from Jira, "Jira epics · 3 of 7 done" opens the list of its epics: each with its key, which opens it in Jira, its title and its Jira status, the open ones first. They are not tasks, so your board stays your own work.

entries.title: Settings › Armarium shows the Jira connection
entries.detail: A new part of Settings, as in folia, for the admin: whether the Jira sync works, the last sync that worked and what it did, when the next one runs, how many goals come from Jira, and the last five runs, a failed one with its reason.

entries.title: A key result's Tasks link opens the board at its row
entries.detail: In Goals, Tasks beside Check in opens the board with a row per key result, as before, and now scrolls so that key result's row stands at the top.

entries.title: Goals can follow a Jira plan
entries.detail: A Jira Strategy is an Objective and an Initiative under it a Key Result; the Epics under an Initiative count as its work, beside the tasks that serve it, and are not made tasks. A synced goal shows its Jira key, which opens the issue. Goals already in tabula are linked by their number or title and keep their tabula names. The sync runs every 30 minutes on tabula's server and never writes to Jira.

entries.title: Blocked by stands right below Epic again
entries.detail: In the task window the order is now Subtasks, Epic, Blocked by, Key result, Comments: what the task is part of and what it waits for come first, then the key result it serves.

entries.title: Key result stands below Epic in the task window
entries.detail: In the task window, creating or editing, the Key result section now comes after Epic and before Blocked by. A task inside an epic serves its epic's key result, so the epic comes first.

entries.title: An epic goes to Done only when its tasks have
entries.detail: As a task with open subtasks cannot go to Done, an epic with an open task cannot either: finish, archive or delete its tasks first, and the app says so. It holds on the card, on the board, in the editor, in bulk edit, for Brain and for a tick in folia. In bulk edit an epic selected together with its open tasks goes to Done after them. A task in it that only another person can see is not counted.

entries.title: Brain sees what you see, and does more and 2 more
entries.detail: Brain sees what you see, and does more: Brain is told which board is on screen, its filters, the task open in its window (or the one you had open a moment ago, since pressing into Ask Claude closes it) and the tasks ticked in Select, so "this task" and "these" mean what you are looking at. It searches every task, done, archived and deleted ones too, and reads a task's comments, blockers and Activity, and the Reports figures. It can add, rename, remove, move and tick subtasks, write a comment, make a task wait for another, set a repeat, archive and restore, and open a task, a board, filters or a saved view when you ask to see something. One Undo still takes back what a reply changed in your tasks. On a phone all header buttons share one row: On a phone the header is the name, then every button on one line, then the search: Undo, Redo and New task, the tools, then the bell and Settings, 3px apart. On a narrow phone the boxes are a little smaller so all of them fit. The tools were spread across a row of their own. The row under the filters is centred: The small pills under the filter buttons now show their text in the middle, like the buttons above them. A count, when there is one, stays at the right edge.

entries.title: Search and Ask Claude look like the header's buttons
entries.detail: The magnifier and the sparkle at the left of the search field are now small soft-amber boxes, like New task and the other header buttons. The mode you are in, search or Ask Claude, is full amber.

entries.title: On the Goals page the header keeps every button
entries.detail: Select, Review and task details no longer disappear on the Goals page. They stay in their place, switched off, so nothing in the header moves when you switch between the board and your goals. A switched-off button keeps its outline but loses its fill and fades, the same as Undo when there is nothing to undo.

entries.title: Select, Review and a bell in the header; Views as a filter · Brain is one panel, with your earlier questions in it
entries.detail: Select, Review and a bell in the header; Views as a filter: Every header button now has the look of New task: a soft amber box that lights up when you point at it and turns full amber while it is on. Undo and Redo stand beside the name, then New task. Select, Review (with the number of tasks waiting) and a bell for For you (with what is unread) moved from under the filters into the header. Views is the last filter button now, after Swimlanes, and opens a menu like the others to open, save or delete a view. The filter buttons are narrower, and each menu is exactly as wide as its button. On a phone the header has a row of its own for the tools, so task details is back there. Brain is one panel, with your earlier questions in it: The conversation window and the microphone are gone. Brain's panel under the search field now holds the whole conversation: your earlier questions stand above the newest, one line each, and a press opens one again with its reply and what it changed. Start over, the circling arrow in the panel's head, begins a new conversation. Settings › Brain › Open opens the panel with the field ready for your question.

entries.title: Brain answers in a panel under the search field
entries.detail: Brain's reply no longer squeezes into the search field. It drops down in a panel underneath, with its paragraphs and lists, and a task code in it opens the task. Under the reply, What it changed lists each change, and Undo takes back what the reply did to your tasks. The panel stays while you type your answer, and goes on Escape, a press outside it or ×.

entries.title: Set a key result on many tasks at once
entries.detail: Select now has a Key result menu after Epic, once you have key results. It lists the ones you are on, under their objective, and No key result. A task someone else owns keeps the key result its owner chose, and the message names it. One Undo takes it all back.

entries.title: Your goals are in the backups
entries.detail: The daily backup, Back up now and the backup file from Export now hold your objectives and key results, with their check-ins. Restoring one puts your goals back as they were, brings back one you removed, and removes those made since. Goals are not in Undo, so tabula backs up your goals as they are now before a restore changes them.

entries.title: Brain knows your goals
entries.detail: Brain, the assistant in the search bar, now sees the quarter's objectives and key results. Ask it to make an objective or a key result, check in with a reading and how confident you are, tie a task to a key result or put it into an epic, or tell you about a quarter. Ask it to review your OKRs and it says what to change, such as a key result that counts output instead of an outcome, and changes nothing unless you ask. Goals are not in Undo, so it makes them only when you ask.

entries.title: Closing a quarter
entries.detail: Close the quarter, on the Goals page, scores each key result from 0 to 1, proposed from how far it got; says how each objective went and what you learnt; and carries what is unfinished into the next quarter as a draft, with your open tasks that served it. A stretch counts as reached at 0.7. Afterwards each goal shows its score and what was learnt, and a score can still be changed in its window.

entries.title: Roadmap
entries.detail: The Goals page shows Objectives or Roadmap. The roadmap draws the quarter's epics as bars across its weeks, from the first date among an epic and its tasks to the last, under the objective whose key result the epic serves; an epic tied to no objective of the quarter shows below when its dates fall in it. The done share of an epic's tasks is filled, a line marks today, and pressing an epic opens it.

entries.title: Reports
entries.detail: Reports, on the Goals page, shows the last 12 weeks: how many tasks got done each week, done and archived ones by the day they were done, and how long tasks took from their first move to Doing to Done, the median of each week. Three figures lead: done this week, done a week on average, and the time in progress. Point at a week, or tab to it, for its numbers; As a table lists them all. The time in progress needs the task history, so it starts the day that history does, and only signed in.

entries.title: Activity: what changed on a task
entries.detail: An open task ends with Activity: who changed its title, status, priority, size, dates, epic or key result, from what to what, and when, newest first, down to when it was made. A run of typing in the title is one line. The database writes it, so a change from another device or another person is there too. Signed in only.

entries.title: Saved views
entries.detail: Views, right after Select under the filters, keeps what the board shows under a name: the filters with their sorts, Kanban or Calendar, and the swimlanes. It opens a window like For you's, which lists each view with what it holds. Open one and all of it comes back at once; the search is left out. While the screen shows a saved view, the button names it. Saving under a name in use replaces that view, the bin deletes one, and twelve is the most. For you's list is drawn in the same cards.

entries.title: Work in progress limits
entries.detail: Settings › General › Kanban board sets the most tasks Backlog, Doing and Pending should hold. A column over its limit shows its count against the limit in amber, such as 4/3, with an amber line under its header; at the limit it stays quiet. Nothing is refused: a card can still be dropped there. With swimlanes each row keeps its own count, and the header turns amber when the whole column is over.

entries.title: Windows without scrollbars
entries.detail: No window draws a scrollbar any more, nor anything in one: what is taller than its box still scrolls with the wheel, the trackpad or a finger. With one window over another, Escape closes the one on top and leaves the one under it open. A window takes the focus when it opens, so Tab moves through the window and not the page behind it. A goal's Notes field is one box, not a box inside a box.

entries.title: Goals with other people
entries.detail: Share an objective with the person button beside its title: everyone on it changes it and its key results, checks in and links tasks. Its maker can open it to everyone, who can then read it, and can say which other objective it supports. A key result can name who answers for it. Mine, Team and Everyone choose which objectives Goals shows, and the work bar counts everyone's tasks. For you tells you when you are added, when someone else checks in, and on Monday when a key result of yours has gone six days without a check-in.

entries.title: Goals: objectives and key results
entries.detail: The target button at the top opens Goals: a quarter's objectives, each with the key results that say how you will know. A key result is a number to move, a milestone, a baseline to measure first, or a line to hold. Check in each week with the reading and how confident you are; tabula keeps every check-in and draws the confidence as a small line. Each key result has two bars: the outcome you read, and the work done in the tasks that serve it. Find a task's key result in its editor by typing a few words, as for Part of (an epic's tasks serve its key result), see it under the card's title, or sort the board by Swimlanes › Key result. Objectives for a later quarter start as drafts.

entries.title: The old addresses are switched off
entries.detail: j4k.pixelina.me and task-001.pixelina.me no longer lead to tabula. Use tabula.pixelina.me. If an icon on your phone's home screen still says j4k, delete it and add tabula again from tabula.pixelina.me.

entries.title: Get the Mac app is now in About
entries.detail: Settings › About tabula now holds the download of the Mac app. In a browser the Mac app part is gone, as it held nothing else. In the Mac app, that part keeps its own switches.

entries.title: People look like folia's notebooks
entries.detail: A person is now a rounded square with one letter on one of folia's ten notebook colours, the same on cards, in the task window, in Share and in Settings. In Settings › Users the admin picks each person's colour, and everyone sees it on shared tasks.

entries.title: Status, Priority, Size, Tag
entries.detail: The fields now come in this one order everywhere: the filter buttons and the line under them, the task window, and the bar for changing many tasks at once. Epic still follows them.

entries.title: A clear plus for a new task · The List view is gone
entries.detail: A clear plus for a new task: The way to make a task is now a soft amber plus beside the name tabula, on the left. Its edge lights when you point at it, and it turns full amber when you press it and while the new task's window is open. The List view is gone: tabula now opens on the Kanban board, or on the Calendar if you chose that in Settings. Review, Archived and Deleted are on no board, so each of them stands in one column of its own when you pick it under Status. Nothing happened to your tasks.

entries.title: A task opens in a window over the board
entries.detail: Editing or creating a task now opens a window on top of the board, and the board, the filters and your place on the page stay as they are. Close it with its x, with a click beside it or with Escape. Undo and Redo are in the window, the fields have their normal size, and subtasks and comments read as a list of rows. On a phone the window fills the screen.

entries.title: Filter by epic · Blocked by moves under Epic
entries.detail: Filter by epic: A fifth filter button, Epic, sits after Size. Tick an epic to see it with its tasks, or No epic for the tasks in none; each choice shows how many tasks it gives, and the tabula logo clears it with the other filters. Its Sort groups the tasks by their epic's number. Under the filters, the buttons now read Select, Review, For you. Blocked by moves under Epic: In a task's editor, Blocked by now sits below the Epic section, just above Comments.

entries.title: The bulk bar follows the filter buttons
entries.detail: When you change many tasks at once, the bar at the foot now lists Tag, Status, Priority and Size in the order of the filter buttons above, then Epic. The first filter button reads Tag: All, singular like the others.

entries.title: Find the epic by typing
entries.detail: Part of and Blocked by no longer list every open task. Type a few letters of the title, or the task's number (12 finds T-012), and the matches appear below, best first, with the letters you typed in bold. Pick one with a click, or with the arrow keys and Enter. Escape empties the search and leaves the task open. The Epic section now sits just above Comments.

entries.title: Change many tasks at once and 2 more
entries.detail: Change many tasks at once: Press Select under the filters, then select tasks with their checkbox, by pressing a card's title, or with All shown. The bar at the foot sets Status, Tag, Priority, Size or Epic on all of them, and one Undo takes it back. A task that cannot take the change, such as one with open subtasks set to Done, is left as it was and named in the message. A task can wait for others: In a task's editor, Blocked by names the tasks it waits for. It offers none that would wait in a circle, and lists the tasks waiting for this one. While one of them is still open, the card shows an hourglass and that task's number: press it to open that task. When the last one is done, the people on a shared waiting task hear of it in For you. Epics: tasks that hold tasks: A task can hold other tasks now. In a task's editor, Part of puts it into another task, and an epic's editor lists its tasks and adds new ones. A card names the epic it is part of, or counts how many of its tasks are done. On the board, Swimlanes › Epic gives each epic a row: drop a card in a row to move it there. One level only: a task in an epic holds no tasks of its own.

entries.title: Type together in subtasks
entries.detail: In a shared task, a subtask's text now changes letter by letter too, with the other person's named cursor, as the title and description do.
